run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T14:02:45Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on frontend-proxy is firing because frontend-proxy recorded error responses in the window, from two distinct sources. (1) A large, short burst: the payment Deployment replaced its only pod at 13:53:07 with no readiness probe on the container, so the old payment pod was deleted at 13:53:10 while the new payment container did not start its gRPC server until 13:54:25 and did not accept a charge until 13:54:58; throughout that gap checkout's PlaceOrder logged no completions and its PaymentService/Charge client spans were errors, frontend returned HTTP 500 for POST /api/checkout, and frontend-proxy logged the corresponding ingress errors. The 5-minute ingress error fraction rose to 0.0255 at 13:56:45 (from 0.00112 at 14:02:45), i.e. the same order as the 0.0222 value in the alert, and the alert start (14:02:45) is about 9 minutes after that burst, consistent with a pending/for condition. (2) A persistent, low-rate trickle of ingress 503s with response flag UC / upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on GET requests to the frontend service, ~3 per 5 minutes (~0.01/s), which predates the payment burst and continues after it, so an error rate remains above the alert's '> 0' threshold. The 503-reset source is not explained by the available evidence (frontend pod not restarted, no frontend spans on the failing traces, no frontend logs). No pre-incident baseline exists in the collected metrics.

claims.text: frontend-proxy error spans over the trailing hour ending 14:18:45: operations 'ingress' 89.21 STATUS_CODE_ERROR and 'router frontend egress' 69.95 STATUS_CODE_ERROR, against 26232.49 and 26248.71 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans; the same failing requests therefore produce both an ingress error span and an egress error span.

Sampled failing traces show frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans with http.status_code 503 / otel.status_code ERROR whose paired 'router frontend egress' spans carry error=true and http.status_code 0 (no HTTP response from the upstream), and those traces contain no 'frontend' service span at all.

frontend-proxy access log at 13:40:48.293Z: 'GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP HTTP/1.1' returned 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} with a 0-byte body; seven further identical 503 UC lines occur between 13:58:35Z and 14:06:01Z on GET /api/products/6E92ZMYYFZ, /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4, /api/cart, /api/data/?contextKeys=assembly, /api/data/?contextKeys=accessories, /api/products/OLJCESPC7Z.

5-minute error increments for frontend-proxy 'ingress' peak at 32.22 in the bucket evaluated 13:55:00 (and 2.22 at 14:00:00, 4.44 at 14:05:00, 4.28 at 14:10:00, 0-5.56 elsewhere); the 5-minute rate series shows ingress traffic steady near 10 spans/s while the ingress error rate peaks at 0.2643/s at 13:56:45 and settles to ~0.007-0.015/s afterwards.

The error share of frontend-proxy ingress spans, computed as increase(errors[5m])/increase(all ingress spans[5m]), was 0.0255 at 13:56:45 and 0.00112 at 14:02:45. The alert's reported current value 0.0222 could not be reproduced exactly because the RequestErrorRate rule is not loaded in this Prometheus.

frontend service error spans are limited to checkout operations: 'POST', 'POST /api/checkout', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' each show 76.67 errors in the 5-minute bucket evaluated 13:57:45 (window 13:52:45-13:57:45) and 0 in every other returned bucket.

checkout service error spans 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' and 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' each show 46.97 errors in that same window (13:52:45-13:57:45) and 0 afterwards, while payment's own error series ('GET', 'dns.lookup', 'tcp.connect') are 0 throughout.

Kubernetes events in otel-demo: Deployment payment scaled up ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 from 0 to 1 at 13:53:07Z and the pod was scheduled/created at 13:53:07Z; at 13:53:10Z container 'payment' on pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 was stopped, that pod was deleted and ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 scaled from 1 to 0.

Pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d was created 13:53:07Z, its container started 13:53:10Z and it is Running/Ready with 0 restarts; frontend-675fd7b5c5-zjtpt and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-sznks were created 13:20:55Z and are Running/Ready with 0 restarts.

ReplicaSets: payment-54499f9786 was created 13:53:07Z with 1 replica and payment-55766d76b9 (created 13:20:55Z) is at 0 replicas, both using image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, i.e. a same-image configuration rollout; all other application ReplicaSets date from 13:20:54-13:20:57Z except flagd-678dcfdc67, created 13:22:49Z with flagd-c47676d99 at 0 replicas.

New payment container logs: 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 13:54:25.571Z and the first 'Charge request received.' at 13:54:58.971Z, i.e. no payment listener for ~75s after the container started at 13:53:10Z and no charge served for ~108s after the old pod was removed.

checkout logs between 13:54:02.802Z and 13:54:58.163Z contain 40 '[PlaceOrder]' lines with no 'payment went through' or 'order placed' line, whereas at 13:53:05Z and 13:53:10Z those success lines are present.

frontend-proxy access log at 13:53:11.285Z and 13:53:12.638Z/Z 12.948Z: 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1' returned 500 via_upstream with a 21-byte body, i.e. the frontend answered with a server error rather than resetting the connection during the payment restart.

Both the payment and frontend Deployments run 1 replica with RollingUpdate maxSurge 25% / maxUnavailable 25%, and their containers define neither a readinessProbe nor a livenessProbe, so a replacement container is treated as available as soon as it is running.

The flagd-config ConfigMap (key demo.flagd.json) sets defaultVariant 'on' for the flag 'paymentUnreachable' ('Payment service is unavailable') and 'off' for all other flags (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure).

The dominant error burst behind the alert is the payment Deployment rollout: with no readiness probe, the old payment pod was removed at 13:53:10 while the replacement's gRPC server did not start until 13:54:25; checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls failed (checkout PlaceOrder and Charge error spans 46.97 in 13:52:45-13:57:45, no PlaceOrder completions in the logs), frontend's /api/checkout returned 500, and frontend-proxy ingress spans recorded those failures, lifting its 5-minute ingress error fraction to 0.0255 at 13:56:45.

Separately from the payment burst, a persistent low-rate source keeps the frontend-proxy error rate above the alert's '> 0' threshold: sporadic ingress 503s flagged UC / upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on GET requests to the frontend service (observed 13:40:48 and 13:58-14:06, about 0.01 errored spans/s), which predate the payment restart and continue after it. No cause is established for these resets; a keep-alive/idle-timeout interaction between the Envoy upstream connection pool and the frontend's Node HTTP server is unverified, since the frontend container produced no log lines and the proxy's upstream settings are not exposed as a ConfigMap.

The alert's start time 14:02:45Z is about 9 minutes after the payment-restart error burst (13:53:07-13:54:58) and about 6 minutes after the 5-minute error fraction had already fallen to 0.00112, which is consistent with an alert that uses a pending/for duration and/or a longer evaluation window; the rule itself is not loaded in this Prometheus, so this timing relationship is unverified.

The 'paymentUnreachable' fault-injection flag being set to 'on' in flagd-config is not supported as the cause of the Charge failures: the checkout Charge errors are confined to the payment pod-restart window and stop once the new pod began serving, and the new payment container logged completed transactions ('Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.') at 13:58:36-13:58:59 while checkout's Charge error series is 0 after 13:57:45. Caveat: the ConfigMap reflects state at 14:22, and change history is not available, so when the flag was set cannot be checked.

A crash or restart of frontend-proxy or frontend itself is not supported: both pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts and were started at 13:20:58-13:20:59, and all 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready at query time.

An error inside the payment application after it started serving is not supported: payment's own error span series are 0 for the whole returned window and the payment container's logs contain no line matching error/fail/refused/unavailable between 13:50:00 and 14:07:04.

Make the payment Deployment rollout stop causing downtime: add a readinessProbe (or startupProbe) on the payment container's port 8080, or set maxUnavailable: 0, so the old payment pod is only removed once the replacement is actually serving gRPC; the same gap exists on the frontend Deployment.
Investigate and, if not intended, clear the fault-injection configuration: flagd-config currently sets paymentUnreachable to 'on' while all other demo flags are 'off'.

Treat the two error sources separately in the alerting/configuration: the RequestErrorRate threshold is 'above 0', so the persistent ~0.1% 503-UC background (Envoy upstream_reset_before_response_started on the frontend upstream) is enough to keep it firing; review the threshold/for duration and the Envoy upstream keep-alive versus the frontend server's keep-alive timeout.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not loaded in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned no rules at all), so the exact expression, evaluation window and pending duration behind the reported value 0.0222 could not be verified; only approximations from traces_span_metrics_calls_total (0.0255 at 13:56:45, 0.00112 at 14:02:45) are available.

The change-history integration is not available, so who or what rolled the payment Deployment at 13:53:07Z (same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment) and replaced the flagd ReplicaSet at 13:22:49Z could not be determined.

Why the replacement payment container needed ~75s to start its gRPC server and ~108s to accept a charge is unknown; no pod events (image pull, probe failures, container restarts) were returned for it and its restart count is 0.

The frontend container wrote no log lines in the window (0 lines read for 13:19:30-14:19:14), so the frontend side of the 503 UC upstream resets could not be inspected; frontend-proxy has no ConfigMap in otel-demo, so its upstream keep-alive/idle-timeout configuration could not be checked.

Jaeger data ends at about 13:46Z (data_as_of 13:46:01Z; a frontend error-trace query for 13:45-14:19 returned no data), so spans for the 13:53-13:55 payment outage are not available and that part of the chain rests on span metrics and pod logs rather than traces.

No pre-incident baseline exists: the earliest sample returned by the 5-minute increase query was 13:35:00Z and all otel-demo pods were created around 13:20:5x, so the error rate before this environment started could not be compared.
Whether the ConfigMap flag values (paymentUnreachable 'on') were the same during the incident window is unknown; Kubernetes objects and ConfigMaps were read at ~14:22Z and reflect current state only.
next_steps: Review the payment Deployment rollout (13:53:07Z) and the flagd Deployment change (13:22:49Z) in the change/deployment history to identify the operator or pipeline responsible.
Add a readinessProbe/startupProbe on the payment and frontend containers, or set maxUnavailable: 0, and re-test a single-replica rollout to confirm zero failed charges during replacement.
Confirm whether flagd's paymentUnreachable=on is intentional in this environment and restore it if not.

Inspect the frontend-proxy (Envoy) upstream cluster configuration and the frontend Node.js keep-alive settings for the sporadic 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started responses, and enable frontend access/error logging so these can be diagnosed.

Re-evaluate the RequestErrorRate alert expression and threshold (currently '> 0') against the known background 503-UC rate so that a single short rollout does not leave the alert firing on residual noise.
